title: The Right Not to Be Saved
narrativeSpine: Effective help does not automatically authorize intervention; legitimate boundaries must explain training, exit, coercion, and their own stopping conditions.
firstSceneDraft: The Right Not to Be Saved examines the authority hidden inside successful help.
This argumentative book distinguishes an intervention's benefit from permission to impose it.
It acknowledges modernity's achievements before questioning what their success authorizes.
Its scope connects restricted knowledge, public institutions, cultural autonomy, and persuasive AI.
visualActionProposal: Open training doorway with a visible path, then a supportive hand stopping before another person’s threshold; bright civic terracotta, teal and saffron.
